methodologyNotes: Roster covers thirteen rolling tool chests / roller cabinets across nine brands (Husky, Milwaukee, Craftsman, Snap-on, Homak, Gladiator, Extreme Tools, Viper Tool Storage, DeWalt, WEN), verified 2026-08-12 primarily against manufacturer-hosted product/spec pages (milwaukeetool.com, homak.com, gladiatorgarageworks.com, extremetools.com, wenproducts.com) with Craftsman, Husky, and Snap-on corroborated via indexed manufacturer/retailer page titles where direct fetch was blocked by bot protection (Home Depot, Lowe's, and several other major retailers returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches all session, so those pages could not be scraped directly even though they are real, live listings). Two seed items could not be verified as real, current products and were corrected rather than guessed: (1) the seed "DeWalt DWST24072" does not resolve to any current DeWalt SKU (absent from DeWalt's own storage-and-organization catalog listing and from every retailer search performed) while the near-identical "DWST24071 — 41 in. Wide 7-Drawer Tool Chest" is real and indexed on dewalt.com, so the entry was corrected to DWST24071. (2) the seed "WEN 5-Drawer" does not correspond to a rolling cabinet in WEN's current lineup (WEN sells almost no wheeled tool storage); the closest real match is the WEN GG261T, a 5-drawer premium tool chest with carrying handles designed to sit atop WEN's separate GG262B rolling base — it is stationary, not itself a rolling unit, and is retained with caster fields left null and this distinction noted in its provenance rather than silently presented as a rolling cabinet. "US General" (Harbor Freight), "Kobalt 3000 Series," "RIDGID Pro Series," and "Montezuma SE Series" from the suggested list were dropped entirely rather than included on unverifiable specs: their retailer/manufacturer pages returned 403/404/JS-shell responses all session and no reliable model number or spec could be confirmed, so two additional real, verified products (a second Milwaukee and a second Craftsman/Gladiator SKU each) were substituted to reach the required count without guessing. total_load_capacity_lb, steel_gauge, caster_load_rating_lb, and weight_lb are left null wherever no fetched source stated the figure for that specific SKU — general per-drawer-slide or product-line figures were not extrapolated onto a specific model's overall rating. Snap-on's own literature states the broader Masters Series line is "rated up to 6,800 lbs" across various configurations; that figure is not attributed to the specific KTL1022APBO1 SKU documented here since no per-SKU total was found, so total_load_capacity_lb is null for that entry. Craftsman CMST82763BK's caster-size text ("3 in. x 1 in. casters") appeared adjacent to a load figure that could not be reliably distinguished from a page-parsing artifact, so caster_load_rating_lb was left null for that entry rather than repeat a possibly-corrupted number. priceUsd is null wherever no manufacturer or dealer page displayed a concrete current price (Milwaukee, Snap-on, and several others sell only through dealer networks or omit consumer pricing from their own pages). accessedAt 2026-08-12 throughout.
